# NodeFile

`c.NodeFile` calls the API's NodeFile group. Files of the object store, deployed
to the host.

### Get

```go
func (s *NodeFileService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	path string,
) (*Response[Collection[FileStatus]], error)
```

Show whether a deployed file holds what osapi wrote.

Compares the file on the host with the record that osapi keeps of what it
deployed: in-sync when they agree, drifted when something changed the file,
missing when osapi deployed the file and it is gone, and unmanaged when osapi
did not deploy the path or undeployed it. A path that is a directory is refused.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/file`, and needs the permission `file:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A deployed file, `go run node_file.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.NodeFile.Get(ctx, target, "/etc/osapi/file-example.conf")
```

### Update

```go
func (s *NodeFileService) Update(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input NodeFileUpdateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[FileUpdateResult]], error)
```

Deploy an object of the object store to a path.

Writes the object at the path with its mode and ownership, and keeps a record of
it. A template object, or content_type template, is rendered first with .Facts,
.Vars and .Hostname. The record keeps the SHA-256 of the object as it was read.
A file that holds the content, mode and owner already, from the same object,
does not change and reports changed: false. osapi client file stale list
compares the object now with that SHA-256, so it shows the deployments whose
object changed since.

It sends `PUT /api/node/{hostname}/file`, and needs the permission `file:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Deploy a file, `go run node_file.go update`:

```go
resp, err := c.NodeFile.Update(ctx, target, client.NodeFileUpdateInput{
	ObjectName: "example.conf",
	Path:       "/etc/osapi/file-example.conf",
})
```

Render a template, `go run node_file.go update-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.NodeFile.Update(ctx, target, client.NodeFileUpdateInput{
	ObjectName: "example.conf.tmpl",
	Path:       "/etc/osapi/file-example.conf",
	Vars:       map[string]string{"port": "8080"},
})
```

### Delete

```go
func (s *NodeFileService) Delete(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input NodeFileDeleteInput,
) (*Response[Collection[FileDeleteResult]], error)
```

Remove a file that osapi deployed.

Removes the file and keeps its record, marked undeployed, so status reports
unmanaged. A path that osapi did not deploy, or deleted already, does not change
and reports changed: false. The object stays in the object store.

It sends `DELETE /api/node/{hostname}/file`, and needs the permission
`file:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Remove a deployed file, `go run node_file.go delete`:

```go
resp, err := c.NodeFile.Delete(ctx, target, client.NodeFileDeleteInput{Path: "/etc/osapi/file-example.conf"})
```
